A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffusionGS and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. All 11 pages of each were inspected; both end with references and neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original object and scene benchmark results, a 25-person user study, component ablations and qualitative generation analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains original benchmarks, user-study results and ablations, and reports additional scene comparisons and depth analyses in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the Gaussian-predicting diffusion denoiser, Transformer architecture, dual decoders, mixed training, RPPC and training losses. Specifying 30 DDIM steps adds implementation detail; it does not establish a changed inference algorithm.

E1.justification: The training and benchmark datasets, real-image examples and text-prompted scenarios are retained. v3 adds a qualitative relative-depth estimation comparison in Figure 8. Renaming scene generation as scene reconstruction does not itself establish additional task coverage.

E2.justification: The scene comparison replaces pixelSplat and GS-LRM in v1 Table 1d with Splatter-Image and Flash3D in v3 Table 1e, retaining pixelNeRF. v3 also adds VistaDream to Figure 7 and PhotoNVS with post-hoc Gaussian fitting to Table 1b/Figure 8. Object comparator membership, including GS-LRM, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new PhotoNVS comparison introduces post-hoc Gaussian fitting, separate inference/fitting time measurements and qualitative rendered-depth comparisons. Existing model training budgets, resolutions and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. The revised split wording and expanded one-input/ten-test-view statement do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds a PhotoNVS view-consistency/depth failure case and a visual RPPC ablation in Figure 8, and supplements the scene mixed-training analysis with numerical gains and a different example. Table 2, the numerical scene RPPC benefit and the generation-diversity analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run counts. The seed-varying generation-diversity demonstration remains; v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Object, user-study and Table 2 values are retained, as are DiffusionGS's scene scores of 21.63 PSNR and 15.87 FID. Scene comparator results are substantially revised: Flash3D reports 20.29/35.03, versus the removed GS-LRM comparison's 18.72/91.55. PhotoNVS adds 15.31/28.30 and 61-second inference plus 2417-second fitting results. v3 also reports scene mixed-training gains of 0.61 dB PSNR and 10.53 FID. These change the comparative evidence, not DiffusionGS's retained benchmark performance.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13, the Gaussian and RPPC definitions, viewpoint constraints and translation-invariance assertion are retained. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, and the new depth illustrations introduce no formal derivation.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds scene reconstruction without a depth estimator and revises the headline scene advantage from 2.91 dB/75.68 FID against GS-LRM to 1.34 dB/19.16 FID against Flash3D. The central contributions of single-stage DiffusionGS, mixed training, RPPC and fast inference remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific explanations attributing scene reconstruction quality to generating trajectory views that produce more structured Gaussian clouds. It also attributes PhotoNVS's post-hoc fitting and depth failures to inconsistent synthesized views and overfitting. v1 contains the broader consistency argument but lacks these specific interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 specifies 30 DDIM steps and states that all evaluations use one input and ten testing views. It removes the 6,894-clip DL3DV training-subset count, SfM camera-pose preparation and user-study blinding/shuffling description, and replaces the pixelSplat split reference with generic standard-split wording. Hardware, training budgets and project-page access information remain.

R1.justification: The broad diffusion/3DGS positioning remains, with a targeted revision emphasizing depth-estimator-free scene reconstruction relative to Flash3D, VistaDream and PhotoNVS. These references, MultiDiff and Denoising diffusion via image-based rendering are added; works including pixelSplat, LucidFusion and SDEdit are removed.

P1.justification: v3 edits the title and author block, revises the abstract and scene-related narrative, shortens the conclusion and gives RPPC analysis a separate paragraph. The section order and most method and object-evaluation prose remain intact, making this a targeted editorial revision.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is rebuilt with depth maps, Figure 7 replaces comparator panels and adds reference views, and a new Figure 8 presents PhotoNVS/RPPC depth comparisons. Table 1 is expanded and rearranged, Table 2 moves, and v1 Figure 8 becomes a compressed Figure 9 with a replaced scene example. Figure 4 also corrects the swapped scene/object decoder labels.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the scene evidence through directly relevant single-view comparators, a PhotoNVS comparison, visual depth/RPPC analysis and a numerical mixed-training result. These make the scene claims better supported. The gains are partly offset by removing data-preparation and user-study details; Flash3D also retains an incorrect reference number in Table 1e. The net improvement is useful but limited.
